As a user, I want the Wabbit app shell to load with a clear header and chat workspace so I know the app is ready.
The app renders a centered 'wabbit' header, an input card, model controls, and an empty response carousel region without requiring API keys at startup.
Browser no-env load on http://127.0.0.1:5174/ and dummy-key load on 5173 rendered the shell with no startup crash.
Keep as baseline behavior during overhaul.
As the app, I want one chat state provider so responses, loading state, model selection, Gemini config, and active carousel index stay coordinated.
ChatProvider initializes default OpenRouter Llama 3.3, empty responses, loading flags, Gemini defaults, and reducer actions for responses, model, config, and active index.
Model selection, Gemini config, response creation, and active carousel index all changed correctly during browser tests.
Keep reducer small; add tests when a test runner is introduced.
As a user, I want the query input to show a prompt and avoid submitting blank text so accidental empty requests are prevented.
The textbox uses the placeholder 'What's your next wabbit hole?'; the send button only renders when query.trim() is non-empty.
Browser test: send button count was 0 when empty, 1 after typing 'hello world', and 0 after keyboard clear. Source scan verifies deprecated onKeyPress was removed in favor of onKeyDown.
As a user, I want to type a question and submit it with Enter or the send button so the selected model returns a response card.

Submit sets loading, stores current query, resolves provider from selectedModel, reads the provider key, calls the registered client, appends a Response, clears input on success, and resets loading. Handled errors render as response cards.

Final mock-mode browser tests on http://127.0.0.1:5181/ submitted typed OpenRouter and Gemini queries, appended response cards, cleared input on success, and produced no console warnings/errors. npm run verify:user-stories now also covers OpenRouter and Gemini provider-client success paths with deterministic fakes. Real provider success calls were unavailable because provider keys are missing.
Real provider success path still needs real keys.
Run one real-key smoke test after provider keys are available.
As a user, I want a dropdown of suggested prompts so I can start quickly without typing.
The chevron button opens three hardcoded recommendations; selecting an item immediately submits that text through handleSubmit as an override query.
Post-fix browser test opened recommendations, selected a canned query, rendered an OpenRouter mock response card, closed the dropdown, and logged no warnings/errors.
Submit-on-select is a product decision risk; there is no edit-before-send step.
Decide whether recommendations should submit or only populate input.
As a user, I want a settings dialog to choose the provider and model used for future chat requests.
The settings icon opens Select Model with OpenRouter and Google Gemini tabs; OpenRouter is selected by default for the default model.
Browser test opened Select Model, saw OpenRouter selected, Google Gemini unselected, and verified closed dialog content is no longer visible after Done.
Keep aria labels on icon controls.
As a user, I want to choose among OpenRouter models so the app can route my next request to that model.
The OpenRouter tab shows three registry-backed radio options and selecting one dispatches SET_MODEL with isGemini=false.
Browser test observed Llama 3.3, DeepSeek R1, and Phi-4; Llama 3.3 was checked by default.
Provider model IDs may drift from live provider catalog.
As a user, I want to choose a Gemini model and see the key requirement so I understand what is needed to use Gemini.
The Gemini tab shows an API-key hint and five Gemini/LearnLM radio options with descriptions; selecting a radio dispatches SET_MODEL with isGemini=true.
Browser test observed five Gemini options and selected Gemini 2.0 Flash-Lite.
Some Gemini IDs are experimental or likely stale.
Validate Google model availability before overhaul implementation.
As a Gemini user, I want to tune temperature, topK, topP, and max output tokens so I can control generation behavior.

The config button appears for the selected Gemini model; the inline config region exposes sliders/input, Apply persists config to context, Done closes the selector, and QueryInput passes config into Gemini generation options.

Post-fix browser test selected Gemini 2.0 Flash-Lite, changed max output tokens to 1234, applied config, verified Done hides the dialog, submitted a query, and verified response text included maxOutputTokens=1234. npm run verify:user-stories verifies Gemini config defaults, clamps, integer rounding, invalid-input fallback, and Gemini SDK option propagation.
Apply persists config but the inline region remains open until Done; current behavior is documented.
Keep exact option propagation covered by the deterministic verifier.
As a developer, I want models defined in one registry so provider filtering and model lookup remain consistent.
modelRegistry stores name/value/provider/description/config; getModelsByProvider filters by provider and getModelByValue resolves the selected model without importing provider implementations.
Source review, selector tests, and npm run verify:user-stories verified registry filtering and lookups. Shared Gemini config types now live in interfaces/core.ts.
Refresh model data as a separate overhaul task.
As a developer, I want provider clients registered behind one interface so UI code can ask for a provider without knowing construction details.
ApiClientRegistryImpl registers gemini/openrouter factories, caches instances by provider and API key, and no provider import throws just because an env key is missing.

No-env browser startup rendered normally. npm run verify:user-stories verified mock registry providers, cache behavior, deterministic mock content, missing-key factory errors, and deterministic provider-client success paths.
Registry still logs when an unknown provider is requested.
Keep registry simple; add unit coverage around cache keys later.
As an OpenRouter user, I want the app to send chat-completions requests with my prompt and selected model.
Client posts to OpenRouter chat completions with system/user messages, selected model, temperature, max_tokens, Bearer auth, and wraps empty/API errors without logging keys.

Final mock-mode OpenRouter query succeeded through the shared registry and rendered markdown/table/code content. No-mock missing-key submit rendered a handled error card. npm run verify:user-stories now asserts the OpenRouter endpoint, model, system/user messages, temperature, max_tokens, Bearer auth header, and returned content using a deterministic axios fake. No successful production call was made because VITE_OPENROUTER_API_KEY is missing.
Production success path needs a real OpenRouter key.
Run one real-key OpenRouter smoke test after VITE_OPENROUTER_API_KEY is available.
As a Gemini user, I want the app to send prompts to Google Generative AI with model configuration defaults.
Client constructs GoogleGenerativeAI with the provided API key, applies model and generationConfig, concatenates systemPrompt when present, and wraps empty/API errors.

Mock-mode Gemini query selected gemini-2.0-flash-lite, passed temperature/topK/topP/maxOutputTokens, and rendered response metadata. npm run verify:user-stories now asserts GoogleGenerativeAI construction, selected model, generationConfig, system/user prompt composition, and returned content using a deterministic SDK fake. No Gemini production call made because VITE_GEMINI_API_KEY is missing.
Production success path needs a real Gemini key.
Run one real-key Gemini smoke test after VITE_GEMINI_API_KEY is available.
As a user, I want responses to appear as cards and see pending state while a normal or topic response is loading.
ResponseList maps responses to ChatResponseCard, appends ResponseSkeleton during loading flags, auto-focuses new responses, and shows arrows/dots when multiple cards exist.

Final delayed mock-mode browser test on http://127.0.0.1:5182/ with VITE_MOCK_API_DELAY_MS=1200 showed Loading response skeleton immediately and mid-delay, then replaced it with the final mock response card with no console errors.
Add mock provider latency tests for skeleton behavior.
As a user, I want response cards to be navigable by arrows, keyboard, drag, and indicators when multiple responses exist.
CardCarousel stacks cards by activeIndex, makes inactive slides inert, supports indicator tabs, Previous/Next buttons, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight, wheel navigation, and header drag.

Final browser tests verified indicator navigation, Previous and Next icon buttons, no document-level horizontal scroll, response-container scrollLeft=0, active-card topic navigation, and inert inactive card state.
Wheel navigation and autoplay were not separately exercised; autoplay is disabled by current ResponseList usage.
Add component-level tests for wheel/autoplay only if those remain in product scope.
As a user, I want each response card to show my query, timestamp, model, and scrollable rendered answer.
ChatResponseCard shows Query or Wabbit Trail label, local time, query/topic title, model row, and MarkdownMessage in a scrollable body.
No-env response cards showed query text, timestamp, selected model, and the handled error response body. Missing API keys no longer inject duplicate card warnings.
Keep rendering independent from topic API availability.
As a user, I want LLM responses to render markdown with headings, code, tables, quotes, links, and copyable code blocks.

EnhancedMarkdown normalizes content, renders react-markdown with GFM, makes headings clickable/keyboard-activatable, adds copy buttons to fenced code blocks, styles tables/quotes/lists, and opens links safely.

Mock-mode markdown fixture rendered headings, a table, and a fenced code block with no leaked node attributes. Copy button is hit-testable; when clipboard write is unavailable, it selects the rendered code block and shows Selected.
Add component tests for headings, code, tables, links, and copy controls.
As a user, I want inconsistent model markdown normalized so responses display consistently.
MarkdownService standardizes underline headings, list markers, tables, script tags, indented/fenced code blocks, and uppercase language tags.

Direct normalizer fixture verified underline headings, list marker spacing, table separator formatting, script stripping, indented-to-fenced code, tilde-to-backtick fences, and uppercase language tag normalization.
HTML safety policy is basic script stripping only; define richer policy during overhaul if HTML remains supported.
Add the normalization fixture to an automated test runner when test infrastructure is introduced.
As a researcher, I want to click a response heading to create a deeper topic-specific Wabbit Trail response.

Markdown heading click uses the response card's original model/provider, sets topic loading, calls generateTopicResponse or fallback generateResponse with researchSystemPrompt, appends topic metadata, and resets loading.

Post-fix browser test clicked the Follow-up topic heading, appended an active Wabbit Trail response, preserved previous query/model context, and logged no warnings/errors. npm run verify:user-stories also covers topic native/fallback/error paths.
Add mock provider response with headings and verify topic metadata/model choice.
As a user, I want provider/setup failures to show as response cards so I can see what failed instead of losing my query.
QueryInput catches provider/setup errors, appends a Response whose body starts 'Error: Failed to generate response', leaves the query available for retry, and resets loading.
Final no-mock browser test on http://127.0.0.1:5183/ rendered exactly one handled missing-key error card with no duplicate MarkdownMessage warning.
No retry button or structured error state yet.
Design explicit error actions before overhaul UI work.
As a developer, I want a fresh checkout to explain missing API keys gracefully so setup issues are recoverable.
A missing provider key should not crash app startup; submitting with a missing key should create a recoverable error response; .env.example should contain placeholders only.

Final no-mock app loaded successfully. Missing-key submit rendered a local provider setup error response. .env.example uses placeholders only; final env check found both VITE_OPENROUTER_API_KEY and VITE_GEMINI_API_KEY missing.
If the previous example key was real, rotation remains outside this repo change.
Rotate/verify any exposed key externally if it was real.
As a developer, I want build and lint scripts to validate the app before overhaul work starts.
npm run build compiles TypeScript/Vite; npm run lint runs the ESLint flat config including .mjs scripts and React hooks rules; strict TypeScript no-unused audit and npm run verify:user-stories pass.

Final npm run build, npm run lint, npx tsc --noEmit --noUnusedLocals true --noUnusedParameters true, npm run verify:user-stories, npm outdated --json, npm audit --json, and stale/deprecated source scans all pass.
Confirm dependency updates before package changes.
